note: OSINT Layer 5 of the TENET5 investigation. For each of the 16 primary-source officer findings cataloged in Layer 4 (officer_of_parliament_findings.json), this layer logs what happened NEXT in the accountability chain: criminal investigation, charges, civil litigation, judicial review, parliamentary committee follow-through, and net enforcement outcome. The layer operationalizes the investigation's core structural thesis — that Canada's accountability architecture produces documentation without enforcement — by tracking specific case trajectories rather than asserting the pattern abstractly.
primary_sources: Parliament of Canada committee reports + concurrence votes
Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions annual reports
News-of-record reporting from CBC, Globe, Toronto Star, La Presse, Canadian Press
Officer of Parliament follow-up reports and addenda

enforcement_types.criminal_investigation: An enforcement agency (RCMP, Sûreté du Québec, local police) opened a formal investigation file.
enforcement_types.charges_laid: Criminal charges were filed against at least one individual named in the underlying finding.
enforcement_types.conviction_or_stay: A charged individual was convicted, acquitted, or had charges stayed.
enforcement_types.civil_suit: A civil proceeding (tort, administrative review, charter challenge) was filed arising from the matter.
enforcement_types.judicial_review: A Federal Court or provincial superior court reviewed an administrative decision connected to the finding.
enforcement_types.parliamentary_study: A Standing Committee or Committee of the Whole studied the matter after the officer's report.
enforcement_types.regulatory_change: A regulation, statutory instrument, or policy was changed in response to the finding.
enforcement_types.no_enforcement: No criminal, civil, or regulatory consequence followed the finding.

findings.subject: SNC-Lavalin DPA pressure
findings.net_outcome_label: Report published; Wilson-Raybould expelled from caucus; no criminal prosecution of anyone in the PMO

chronology.detail: House Standing Committee on Justice and Human Rights (JUST-136) — Wilson-Raybould testified; transcript is primary evidence.
Wilson-Raybould and Jane Philpott expelled from Liberal caucus. No court action by either; separate civil actions not filed.
RCMP confirmed to media it was 'examining' the matter; no formal obstruction-of-justice investigation opened. Confirmed via CBC 2019-09-12 and Globe 2021-07-26.
As of April 2023 (when Lucki retired), no RCMP formal investigation or charges had been laid in connection with the Trudeau II finding.
Underlying SNC-Lavalin charges: Quebec Superior Court ruling 2019-12-18 stayed the fraud charges against SNC-Lavalin Group Inc. via a settlement; corporate guilty plea for ~$280M fine.

summary.pattern_summary: Across 16 primary-source officer-of-Parliament findings spanning 2017-2026, zero named public officials have been criminally prosecuted. One civil class action (Phoenix) settled for ~CAD 13M. One active criminal investigation (ArriveCAN / GC Strategies) has not produced charges after two years. The Emergencies Act invocation was held unlawful by the Federal Court in January 2024; the government is appealing. The observable pattern is regulatory_change + no_enforcement — when follow-through occurs, it takes the form of a new regulation or policy announcement, not accountability for specific individuals named in the finding. This is the empirical content of the investigation's 'accountability without enforcement' thesis.
summary.interpretive_note: The 'regulatory_change' count may understate the actual durability of reforms — some Treasury Board spending-control announcements have historically been reversed quietly in subsequent budgets (as tracked by PBO reports). Readers should treat each regulatory_change entry as evidence of announced change rather than implemented change until a follow-up audit confirms otherwise.

liril_audit_summary.methodology: Each finding's full chronology was passed to LIRIL via the mercury.infer endpoint on NATS 4223. The model returned a VERDICT: PASS|WATCH|FAIL with a single-line REASON. PASS = no inconsistency detected; WATCH = firmer source anchoring would help; FAIL = a specific date/cite/outcome appears wrong. This does not verify against the live internet — it only flags inconsistencies the model's training recognizes.
